Gielen, D.J. (1997). Technology Characterisation for Ceramic and Inorganic Materials: Input data for Western European MARKAL. Report ECN-C--97-064, Netherlands Energy Research Foundation ECN, Petten, September 1997. MATTER project (MATerials Technologies for CO2 Emission Reduction), ECN project 7.7018.

Locators are the printed page numbers (PDF page number equals the printed page number). Main file: every MARKAL process table of Chapter 2 (ammonia, bricks, cement and blended cements, tiles, chlorine, concrete, glass, gypsum, kaolin, nitric acid, phosphor, phosphoric acid, potash, quicklime, sand-limestone, soda, salt, stone, sulphuric acid, TiO2) plus the oven-type tables (cement preheaters Table 2.3.1, lime kilns Table 2.13.1, chlorine cells Table 2.5.2, glass melting survey). Each table has columns 2000, 2020 and 2050; a separate process is written per year only where an energy, emission or cost value differs from the previous written year (suffix ", YYYY" in the process name). Costs are per t annual capacity, ECU 1994 (stated), with no cost basis stated and product-output capacity; the author calls them estimates (p.10), many are own guesses based on other sectors. Energy is final energy per t product as MARKAL input: ammonia gas includes feedstock; heat and steam inputs are low-temperature (LT) unless noted; electricity is shown in GJ (0.1 GJ/t = 27.8 kWh/t). Heating-value basis never stated. Cost rows for CCS options: investment barely changes while fixed O&M rises (cement 5 to 80), so capture cost sits in O&M; marked INCLUDES CAPTURE. Traps: Table 2.5.3 fixed O&M printed 100/10/100 (2020 value probably a typo); Table 2.3.5 output labelled "Portland cement" but is clinker; Table 2.13.1 dolomite minimum printed MJ/t. Chapter 3 (materials efficiency options: fertilisers, light-weight bricks, high-strength concrete, cullet recovery, re-use) has no technology data and was not loaded. Inputs without a commodity term (ammonium sulphate, felspar, water glass, gravel, ore) are not loaded as flows. New commodity terms used in flows: cullet, sand, soda-ash, sulphur, rutile. Western Europe, year 2000-2050 projections; the energy values for 2000 are fleet averages, not best available technology.
